reviews.review_msg: Wendi made me reconsider whether or not I wanted to become a teacher. Every question I had about the program or about the 401 course she co-taught, she reacted negatively and made me feel like I was bothering her. I struggled in some ways through 401 as Wendi only wants things done her way. My accessibility needs were not respected during 401 also.

Wendi is directly responsible for the SFU PDP ITEM program no longer running as of 2026. Due to her lack of preparedness, disorganization and inability to run a field school program in a responsible way, students were robbed and hospitalized when the program last ran. Wendi should not be mentoring Teacher Candidates and should not be an FA.

Wendi was tough to work with as a teacher candidate. She kept pushing her way of doing things and taught in a way that does not match the realities of BC classrooms. I have not had a single good experience with her, and any questions were taken as criticism of her. I had difficulty with the program as well, partially because of her. Not a good FA.

Wendi comes across as very militant with her views and is unwilling to consider other points of view. I had to redo many of my resources I made for my practicum as she did not approve of them. When I showed my peers and other teachers they said they were great. I do not think she is a great FA and a poor fit to guide junior teachers.

I agree with the other reviews. Some of the other TCs had better FAs and thus did not have such a bad time as I did in the program. My biggest complaint is how Wendi gives no warning for half of the program changes and just forces you to go along with it, or she takes it out on you. Her feedback and lectures were not useful to my development.

A teaching degree like PDP is dictated by how lucky you are. If your SA or, in Wendi's case, FA, is no good, you will have a very rough time. My time with Wendi has not been good. I did not learn much from her, and she constantly made excuses for herself. She is critical of things that fall outside the BCTC standards.

I really did not enjoy working with Wendi. Whenever I asked a question about the course or program in general, she would treat it as criticism. When I asked questions about the feedback I received, she would also react negatively and say I was being defensive when I was only asking for details on my feedback. Not a great mentor for junior teachers.

I did not enjoy working with Wendi. Whenever I asked a question about the course or program in general, she would treat it as criticism. When I asked questions about the feedback I received, she would also react negatively, saying I was being defensive when I was only asking for details about my feedback. Not a great mentor for junior teachers.

I also did not enjoy working with Wendi during my time in PDP. Wendi came across as very uncompromising and expected us to always be ready to change to her way of doing things, even when her way did not align with BCTC standards. She is an activist more than a teacher and only cares about what is easy, not what is best for her students.

I had a really tough time in EDUC 401 as I did not get the support I needed to succeed. Wendi was always placing the onus on me to do anything extra and always did the bare minimum. She took course questions as program criticisms, and was very difficult to talk to. Overall, my experience with her as my FA has been negative, and I regret taking PDP.

It is baffling to me why SFU has people like Wendi in programs meant to mentor and help new and returning teachers. I already have teaching experience, and Wendi focused way too much on being an activist rather than ensuring my students' success. None of her feedback was meaningful and seemed like box-checking to please her. She was rude to me too.

Wendi was not helpful when I got placed with a bad supervising teacher. I went through 6 weeks of difficulty without any support. She told me to practice being responsive, and that I did not take feedback well; it was only after I went above her and complained that something was done. More interested in her research than her students' well-being.

I did not have a good practicum, as my first teacher was not a good match. Despite clearly documenting the issues I was having, Wendi threw many of the issues on me and said I was not reflecting enough. She asked irrelevant questions and talked down to me during the meetings she called with very little notice. She is not a supportive FA.

Wendi was my FA for EDUC 400. She called several day of meetings, and was accusatory toward me and painted my questions to my teachers in a negative light. She made constant excuses for PDP ITEM and the lack of documentation and preparedness the program had. I am not surprised it was cancelled. Wendi often says one thing, then does another. Beware.

Wendi was my FA for 401, and when I had issues with my teacher at my school, she was very condescending and acted like I was the problem. Only when I got outside help did she soften her approach and pretend to be supportive. I will never forget her trying to blame me for the issues my teacher caused in my class. If you get her as your FA, be wary.

Only when I got outside help did she soften her approach and pretend to be supportive. I will never forget her trying to blame me for the issues my teacher caused in my class. If you get her as your FA, be wary.

Wendi is not pleasant to talk to and has a tendency to talk down to people when they ask her questions. My EDUC 401 class had her as the co-teacher, and I dreaded asking her questions as she refused any effort to make the program more accessible. She always acted like my needs were a chore and did bare minimum. Overly obsessed with her research.

Wendi has not replied to my requests for course outlines for EDUC 400/401 she co-taught. This will cause issues for me when I am evaluated for certification in my home country. She has not replied to emails about adding our names to Colleen's WestCAST presentation so we can get credit for presenting, even though she presented. Not a helpful FA.

Wendi is incredibly militant. When I had concerns about how class was being delivered, she claimed I was not being adaptable to the PDP program. She likes stopping people in the hallway and threatening them with disciplinary meetings if they are unable to attend for health reasons. She loves micromanaging students forcing them to do things her way.

I have never had a single positive conversation with Wendi as my co-teacher. She expects compliance in all things PDP related, and is completely unwilling to compromise on anything. She enabled Colleen in EDUC 400 when several of us had concerns about the lack of preparedness for the ITEM program. An FA should have your back, Wendi does not.

Wendi was the co-teacher for my EDUC 400 class. She constantly made excuses for why EDUC 400 was always running things last minute, and was very condescending whenever I had questions about PDP or how EDUC 400 was run. She expects her students to adapt to her course with no notice, which made class really hard. Bad luck if you get her as your FA.
